bodyText:
Muse is the strongest consumer AI agent launch to date, and the early engagement data is exceptional. Launched on Sep 8, 2026, Meta’s personal AI agent Muse reached #1 on both the US App Store and Google Play within two weeks, overtaking ChatGPT. Sensor Tower estimates 2.6mn downloads in the first 13 days, while Apptopia puts US mobile DAU at 642k versus ChatGPT’s 231k at the same post-launch stage in 2023. A dedicated per-user cloud VM, background task execution, and US$20/US$100 monthly tiers make Muse the first consumer agent with real mainstream traction. It is also the clearest product-level evidence so far that Meta’s US$130–145bn 2026 capex is producing something consumers actually want. The product is good. We have no debate there.
However, we are not comfortable with the stock’s recent rally. Meta shares rose 11.4% on Sep 21. As of Sep 24, the stock traded at 22x 12-month forward earnings, near the upper end of its one-year valuation range, 43% above its March low and approaching an all-time high. At this level, Muse can no longer just be a good product. It needs to become a large, durable and monetizable platform. Retention is still unproven, transaction access remains fragmented, and revenue contribution is minimal today. A range of estimates we see point to at most 20-30% incremental profit over a few years.
Ultimately competition will intensify among ecosystems and “giants”. Amazon’s decision on Sep 20 to block Muse at checkout is the first clear example of where consumer agents may run into structural resistance. We also suspect Gemini + Apple and labs like OpenAI could launch similar efforts soon – yes, Meta has unmatched distribution, but we are just highlighting a direction here. When competing products come in, sentiment could weaken on the stock.
Things may get worse before they get better. Agent workloads are materially more expensive than chat, requiring persistent cloud infrastructure, browser execution, tool calls and verification layers. Meta is already showing constraint in compute as of this writing. Meta is also subsidizing adoption through free tokens and VM capacity while maintaining a high level of capex investment. While traction and related revenue generated from Muse could help its top-line, incremental profit may be limited vs its subsidies considering competition. If consumer agents are such an attractive opportunity, we see more of a reason that competition will be just as aggressive.  
Downgrade to Underperform: We maintain our forecasts and US$700 TP, but downgrade Meta to Underperform, as the stock now trades above our TP and faces potential short-term catalysts upcoming as mentioned above. We think Muse is interesting over the long-term so this may just be a tactical short opportunity.  
Risks:  faster-than-expected monetization from Muse to deliver earnings beat. Rating: UNDERPERFORM, Current Price: US$751.66, Target Price: US$700.00, Market cap: US$1,915bn
